blockers.description: Upstream lerobot async_inference deadlock: PolicyServer's _obs_sanity_checks()/observations_similar() skips running inference on any observation whose joint-space state is nearly identical (~1 degree tolerance) to the last one it actually processed, unless a must_go flag forces it through. Because the robot wasn't moving (initially due to the now-fixed staleness bug below), every subsequent observation looked unchanged to the server, so it silently discarded them instead of running inference -- explaining 0% GPU utilization and an action queue that never refreshed after the first chunk. Matches open, unresolved upstream GitHub issues: huggingface/lerobot#2356 ("AsyncInference only running one action chunk"), #2374 ("SmolVLA freezes and barely fluctuates around neutral" on SO-101), #1500 ("Observation #0 has been filtered out", names the exact mechanism). No confirmed upstream fix exists as of this research.
blockers.workaround: Not yet applied/verified. Working theory: now that both local bugs are fixed, the very first real action may arrive fast enough to pass the corrected STALE_ACTION_S=3.0s threshold and cause genuine robot motion, which would make subsequent observations genuinely differ in joint-space and break the deadlock naturally -- untested, needs a fresh live retry. If that doesn't work, the deadlock may need addressing more directly (e.g. investigating whether the client's `must_go` flag is actually reaching the server as expected, or whether the server's own observation_queue maxsize=1 is dropping non-must_go observations regardless).

decisions.decision: Fixed connect_bridge() in control/vla_bridge/robot_client.py to explicitly start the library's receive_actions() background thread (as a daemon thread, with client.start_barrier downsized to 1 party since the library's own control_loop() partner thread is deliberately never run here, per T-11-09's safety-validator-bypass avoidance).
decisions.rationale: Live testing found action_queue was permanently empty -- an entire 22-step episode ran with the robot never moving because nothing was pulling computed actions off the gRPC stream. receive_actions() never calls robot.send_action() itself, so starting it doesn't reintroduce the T-11-09 bypass. Commit 343fa28.

decisions.decision: Fixed pop_validated_action()/validate_action() in control/vla_bridge/robot_client.py and control/vla_bridge/safety_validator.py so the bridge path checks action staleness against STALE_ACTION_S (3.0s, defined specifically for network round-trip latency) instead of STALE_OBSERVATION_S (1.0s, meant for a synchronous local loop). Added an explicit stale_threshold_s parameter to validate_action() (default STALE_OBSERVATION_S, unchanged for existing synchronous callers).
decisions.rationale: After the receive_actions() fix, real actions started arriving in the queue but every single one was being rejected as stale under the 1.0s synchronous threshold, which a real cloud round-trip (tens of seconds, worse on a cold-started policy server) can never meet. STALE_ACTION_S already existed in the code with a comment saying it was 'used by a later plan's bridge path' (i.e. this plan) but was never actually wired in. Commit e55aa53. Note: 3.0s is still an unvalidated starting guess, not yet confirmed against a real warm-server round-trip measurement -- a real warm round-trip time was never obtained this session because the deadlock below prevented a second chunk from ever being computed.

decisions.decision: Also fixed BridgeActionSource.get_action() to surface pop_validated_action()'s flags (e.g. "no action available, holding position", "stale observation...") through model_version instead of silently discarding them.
decisions.rationale: Before this fix, an empty-queue hold and a genuine valid action were indistinguishable in episode.jsonl (both logged as '@unknown') -- this hid the real diagnostic signal that led to finding both bugs above. Commit 343fa28.

decisions.decision: Diagnosed (via live testing + reading installed lerobot source + web research) but did NOT attempt to patch: PolicyServer's observation-similarity filter causing a motion deadlock.
decisions.rationale: This is upstream library behavior (lerobot.async_inference.policy_server), not this project's code -- patching it would mean monkey-patching or vendoring a fix into an installed third-party package, a bigger decision than a live-verification session should make unilaterally. Matches unresolved upstream issues huggingface/lerobot#2356, #2374, #1500. Deferred to next session's retry to see if the two already-applied fixes are sufficient to avoid triggering it in practice.
